what_its_for: Teriparatide is used to treat osteoporosis (weak, brittle bones) in men and women who are at high risk of breaking a bone. It works by acting like a natural hormone in your body called PTH (parathyroid hormone) to help your body build new, stronger bone. It is often used when other osteoporosis medicines have not worked well enough or cannot be used.
how_to_take: Teriparatide comes as a liquid solution in a pre-filled injection pen. You give yourself one small injection under the skin (subcutaneous) in your thigh or belly (abdomen) once a day. Your doctor or nurse will teach you how to use the pen correctly before you start. Always inject in a slightly different spot each day to avoid skin irritation. Sit or lie down when you give yourself the injection, especially for the first few doses, because some people feel dizzy or lightheaded afterward. Stay sitting or lying down for a few minutes after each injection.
dosing: The usual dose is 20 micrograms (mcg) injected once a day under your skin. Treatment is typically limited to a maximum of 2 years (24 months) over your lifetime. Do not use teriparatide for longer than your doctor has prescribed. After stopping, your doctor will likely switch you to another bone-strengthening medicine to maintain your bone gains.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. However, if it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next regular dose on schedule. Never take two doses in one day to make up for a missed one. Try to take teriparatide at the same time every day to help you remember.
storage: Keep your teriparatide pen in the refrigerator at 36°F to 46°F (2°C to 8°C) at all times. Do not freeze it — if it accidentally freezes, throw it away and get a new pen. After each use, put the pen cap back on and return it to the refrigerator right away. Do not leave the pen at room temperature for extended periods. Each pen can be used for up to 28 days after the first use. After 28 days, throw the pen away even if medicine is still left inside. Store the pen without a needle attached. Dispose of used needles safely in a sharps container.
what_to_avoid: Avoid standing up too quickly right after your injection, as this can cause dizziness or fainting, especially when you first start using this medicine. Avoid drinking too much alcohol, as it can weaken your bones and increase your fall risk. Do not use teriparatide if you have ever had radiation therapy involving your bones, have Paget's disease of bone, have high calcium levels in your blood, or have bone cancer or cancer that has spread to your bones. Talk to your doctor before taking calcium or vitamin D supplements, as adjustments may be needed.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: leg cramps, muscle weakness, or numbness and tingling (possible signs of low or high calcium); fast or pounding heartbeat; dizziness or feeling faint, especially after injecting; severe nausea or vomiting; unusual bone pain; a lump, swelling, or pain near a bone (possible rare sign of bone tumor called osteosarcoma); signs of high calcium such as nausea, vomiting, constipation, muscle weakness, or confusion; or any allergic reaction such as rash, itching, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing.
when_it_works: Teriparatide starts building new bone relatively quickly, but you may not feel any different day to day since stronger bones do not cause noticeable symptoms. Your doctor will monitor your bone density with a DEXA scan (a special bone X-ray) over time to check how well the medicine is working. Some improvement in bone density can be seen within 3 to 6 months, with the best results seen after 18 to 24 months of treatment. Be patient and take your medicine every day for the best results.
special_populations: Older adults: Teriparatide can be used safely in older patients, but be extra careful about dizziness and fall risk after injections. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Teriparatide should NOT be used during pregnancy or while breastfeeding. Tell your doctor right away if you become pregnant. Kidney problems: Use with caution if you have moderate to severe kidney disease; your doctor will decide if this medicine is safe for you. Children and teenagers: Teriparatide is not approved for use in children or young adults whose bones are still growing. Cancer history: If you have ever had bone cancer or have received radiation to your bones, teriparatide is not safe for you.
